cards.text: Akasaka backstreets — Behind Akasaka Biz Tower: a dense grid of alleys packed with izakaya, premium yakiniku, ramen and a few themed places. Five minutes from the hotel, which is the whole point on landing night. No booking needed if you go early. 18 Oct · walk-in Lunch · Shibuya

Nonbei Yokocho — "Drunkards' Alley" — two lanes of tiny post-war shacks wedged against the Yamanote tracks, most seating six people. Famous after dark, but a few open early for ramen and yakitori, and it's far more atmospheric at lunch than anything in the station. Best after dark · any Tokyo evening Breakfast · if you stay

Tsukiji outer market — The wholesale auction moved to Toyosu but the outer market is still here and still the best breakfast in the city — tamagoyaki on a stick, uni straight from the tray, grilled scallops, and knife shops worth an hour on their own. Go by 09:00. 20 Oct · Tokyo-deeper track Evening · Shinjuku

Omoide Yokocho & Golden Gai — Two survivals of post-war Tokyo a few minutes apart: "Memory Lane" for smoke-blackened yakitori counters, Golden Gai for two hundred bars in six alleys, most seating five. Some charge a cover for non-regulars — look for the English welcome signs. 20 Oct · after the free observation deck If you go to Fuji

Depachika & ekiben — The basement food halls under any department store are the best-value quality food in Japan — and the way to feed six people fast. Useful throughout, and the way to stock a picnic for the Fuji drive rather than on the train. Any day · best under Shinjuku or Nihombashi See every dish across the trip → ← Overview Next · Miyakojima →

rows.title: Group dinner · Akasaka, 20 Oct
rows.text: The Kyoto party gets back around 22:15 and the Fuji party around 20:00. A late booking lets whoever is back eat together.
rows.book: Ask the hotel front desk to book — Via Inn Prime Akasaka sits in the middle of the izakaya quarter and they will know what takes six at short notice.

cards.title: Kabuki-za · single act
cards.sub: 一幕見席 · bought on the day
cards.text: You do not have to commit to four hours of kabuki. Hitomaku-mi single-act tickets are sold on the day at the theatre’s side entrance and get you one act. It is the cheapest genuinely extraordinary hour in Tokyo, and if it turns out not to be for you, you have lost the price of a coffee.
cards.book: Ten minutes from Akasaka. Check the day’s programme in the morning and go for whichever act reads best.
cards.when: Good for the 19th, or the evening of the 20th once everyone is back from Fuji and Kyoto.
cards.meta: Cost: ≈ ¥1,000–2,000 · Length: 30–90 min · Book: no — same day · Where: Ginza

cards.title: Sumo morning practice
cards.text: Worth knowing before anyone gets their hopes up: Tokyo’s grand tournaments are January, May and September — there is none while you are here. What you can do instead is watch a stable’s morning practice, which is closer, quieter and arguably the better experience.
cards.book: Goes through a guide or the hotel concierge; stables do not take direct bookings from visitors. Strict etiquette — silence, no crossed legs, no leaving early.
cards.when: Only realistic on the 19th, and only for whoever will genuinely get up for it.
cards.meta: Cost: ≈ ¥10,000–15,000 · Start: very early · Book: through a guide

cards.title: Street go-karting
cards.text: The one Tokyo activity that requires an IDP — which every driver here is carrying anyway for the two car hires. Costumes, public roads, Shibuya and the Rainbow Bridge. Ridiculous, and unlike anything else on this trip.
cards.book: Book ahead and upload licence details in advance; operators will not let you drive without the physical IDP on the day.
cards.when: Four of you will love this and two probably will not — a good candidate for splitting the evening.
cards.meta: Cost: ≈ ¥10,000 · Length: ~2 hrs · Needs: International Driving Permit

cards.title: teamLab Planets TOKYO
cards.text: The one to do if you only do one. You go barefoot and wade through warm knee-deep water under projected koi, then stand inside a mirrored room of hanging orchids. It is a physical experience, not a screen you look at.
cards.book: Timed-entry tickets, online only, through the official store. Wear or bring shorts — you roll trousers up and the water is knee-deep. Bags go in lockers and phones survive fine.
cards.when: Book as soon as the 20 October split is settled. Slots genuinely sell out, and tickets for a given month go on sale roughly a month ahead.
cards.meta: Length: 75–90 min · You get: wet to the knee · Price: from ≈ ¥3,800 · Open until: end of 2027

cards.title: teamLab Borderless TOKYO
cards.text: The other Tokyo venue, and a different proposition: works wander between rooms and spill into each other, with no fixed path. Bigger, longer, and better if you have already done Planets — but less of a single physical hit.
cards.book: Timed-entry tickets online. Entrance is at Azabudai Hills — take the D elevator down to B1, which is not obvious from the street.
cards.when: Same as Planets. If you can only fit one and it is a first visit, take Planets.
cards.meta: Length: 2–3 hours · Format: no map, no route · Price: from ≈ ¥3,800 · Shoes: stay on

cards.title: Shibuya Sky
cards.sub: needs a slot — the 19th is full
cards.text: The rooftop deck over Shibuya Crossing. The 19th now runs shrine-to-Senso-ji with no gap, so this needs its own slot — the honest options are a sunset slot instead of Asakusa on the 19th, or working it into the 20th. The free Metropolitan Government deck in Shinjuku is the no-booking fallback.
cards.book: Timed-entry tickets online. Sunset slots go first and cost more.
cards.when: A week or two ahead is usually enough, except for sunset slots.
cards.meta: Height: 229 m · View: 360° · Best at: sunset

rows.title: Japan Series, if it lands
rows.text: Late October is exactly when the Japan Series runs, and Tokyo Dome is twenty minutes from Akasaka. A Japanese baseball crowd is one of the great sporting experiences anywhere — relentless, organised, brass-band loud, and nothing like a Western stadium.
rows.book: Tickets are hard if it does land on the 18th or 19th, but worth ten minutes of trying. Resale sites are the realistic route.
rows.when: Check the fixture list once the Climax Series finishes in mid-October.
rows.meta: When: late October · Where: Tokyo Dome · Odds: fixture-dependent

cards.text: Hoto, and Fujizakura beer — Hoto is the dish to have — nothing like udon despite appearances, and exactly right after a cold morning at the lake. The local Fujizakura Kogen brewery does a very good weizen if anyone wants a beer with the view. Lunch near the station Group of six

rows.text: Hoto noodles — Yamanashi's mountain dish and nothing like udon: flat, thick, unsalted wheat noodles simmered straight into a miso broth with pumpkin, taro and mushrooms until the whole pot goes thick. Served in an iron cauldron. Exactly right after a cold morning at the lakes. 20 Oct · Kawaguchiko Practical
The highway bus (¥2,200) and the JR-via-Otsuki route exist, but a timetable is exactly what this day is better without.

This is the one day worth checking before you commit. The Fujigoko live webcams are pointed at the mountain from Kawaguchiko, and the forecast is usually honest about cloud. If Fuji is hidden, the day loses most of its point — switch to the Tokyo track and keep everyone's money. The van makes that call cheap: Toyota rentals cancel free before pickup, which prepaid train seats do not.

You are just before the peak — The Momiji Corridor's maple festival on the lake's north-west shore normally runs from early November, so late October catches it turning rather than fully lit. The kokia at Oishi Park are red now, though, and the higher slopes have colour. Colour rises with altitude Eat

Why the van wins here — Six people make the arithmetic lopsided: one van costs about half of six train tickets, and it is the only way to reach Motosuko and the quiet west-lake shores without building the day around a bus timetable. Picking up at Hachioji is the trick — you never drive a metre of central Tokyo, and dropping the van there on the way home puts you on a train while the expressway queues into the city. Worth

Stay for sunset — Fuji turns pink for a few minutes just after the sun drops — the locals call the snow-lit version "beni Fuji". If the sky is clean at 16:00, push the return train back an hour. You will not regret it. Sunset around 17:00 in late Oct ← Tokyo, 20 October Compare · the Kyoto day →

Morning beats afternoon — Cloud builds around the summit as the ground warms, so the mountain is most reliably clear early. That is the argument for the 08:30 train rather than a leisurely start — and for doing Chureito first, before the light flattens. Aim to be at the pagoda by 11:00 Autumn

cards.text: Chureito's 398 steps — They are steep and they are the reason some people skip it. There is a gently sloped path from the same car park that gets to the same viewpoint without a single step — ask for the "slope route". Worth knowing before anyone talks themselves out of it. Arakurayama Sengen Park Timing

cards.title: Kawaguchiko Tenjozan ropeway
cards.text: Up to a deck looking straight across the lake at the mountain, with short trails at the top if legs allow.
cards.book: Tickets on site, no advance booking needed.
cards.when: Nothing to do in advance.
cards.meta: Ride: 3 minutes · From: beside the station

cards.text: Miyako soba — 宮古そば Thick, udon-like wheat noodles in a lighter, ramen-ish broth under fall-apart stewed pork ribs — and traditionally the meat is hidden under the noodles, a local quirk. The famous shops close when the pot runs out, so this is really a lunch dish. Koja Soba is the long-standing name. Go by 11:00 · 25 Oct is your window The big night

Umibudo & the island plate — 海ぶどう "Sea grapes" — a seaweed of tiny green spheres that burst with salt water like caviar, served with ponzu. Alongside: goya champuru (bitter melon stir-fried with tofu, egg and pork), rafute (belly pork simmered in awamori), and gurukun , the Okinawan prefectural fish, deep-fried whole. Any izakaya The local spirit

Awamori — 泡盛 Okinawa's rice spirit — distilled rather than brewed, made with long-grain Thai rice and black koji, and older than shochu. Miyako has its own distilleries: Taragawa , Chuko and Ikema . Ask for kūsu , aged three years or more, which is far smoother. Sort your driver out first. Distillery visits on the 25th The right first night

Izakaya with live sanshin — 三線 The sanshin is Okinawa's three-stringed snakeskin banjo and the ancestor of the shamisen. Several Hirara izakayas run live sets nightly, usually ending with everyone up dancing kachāshī. It is not a tourist performance — it's how the island socialises. Book, especially in season. 21 or 24 Oct · reserve Timing note
Miyako soba crawl — the one day a queue at 11:00 is no hardship

rows.text: Miyako beef — 宮古牛 Rarer than Ishigaki beef and barely leaves the island. Have it as yakiniku, as seared nigiri, or in the beef yakisoba the izakayas do particularly well. This is the 24th's group dinner — book it. 24 Oct · reserve ahead Order it everywhere

What's out of season — Miyako mango is the island's most famous export but the season runs June to August — by late October the farm stands are selling jam, juice and soft-serve rather than fruit. Yukishio salt soft-serve is the year-round consolation, and it's genuinely good. Manage expectations See every dish across the trip → ← Tokyo Next · Kakunodate →

cards.title: Yukishio Salt Museum
cards.text: Holds a Guinness record for the most minerals in a salt. That sounds like nothing until you taste it next to ordinary salt. Short free tour, and the salt soft-serve is much better than it has any right to be.
cards.book: No booking. Drop in on the 25th on the way to or from Ikema — it is right on that road.
cards.when: Buy the salt here; it is the best small souvenir on the island.
cards.meta: Cost: free · Length: ~20 min · Where: northern tip, near Ikema

cards.title: Awamori distillery
cards.text: Okinawa’s rice spirit, distilled on the island. The aged kusu is nothing like the harsh young awamori that puts people off it — closer to a soft rum. Both Taragawa and Ikema pour.
cards.book: Ring ahead if you want the tour rather than just the shop counter; the tasting itself is walk-in.
cards.when: Nominate a driver. Two cars makes this easy — the drinkers go in one.
cards.meta: Cost: free–¥1,000 · Length: ~45 min · Where: both near Hirara

cards.text: Taragawa or Ikema distillery — awamori tasting, nominate a driver

Stars, with almost nothing in the way — 星空 Once you are five minutes out of Hirara there is effectively no light pollution , and late October gives you long dark evenings. You can simply drive out and look up for free — or take a guided night tour for ¥4,000–5,000, which adds the island’s wildlife and someone who knows what you are pointing at. Best on the 25th, after the bridge at golden hour Two of them pour

rows.text: Shigira Ougon Onsen — the largest hot spring in Okinawa, and better in bad weather than good
Miyakojima City Museum — island history and the old Ryukyu tax stone

cards.text: 17-END — 17エンド At the end of Shimoji airport's runway 17: at low tide the sea pulls back to leave a vast shallow lagoon of impossibly pale blue with a sandbar running out into it. At high tide it's just sea. Check the tide table before you drive out — this one is entirely timing. Shimoji · low tide only Quietest

Irabu Ohashi — 伊良部大橋 · 3,540 m The longest toll-free bridge in Japan, curving out over water that shifts through four shades of blue as you cross. Drive it at golden hour, then stop at Makiyama Observatory on the far side and look back at what you just drove. 5 min · do it more than once Best headland

Cape Higashi-Hennazaki — 東平安名崎 A two-kilometre spine of land running into open ocean with sea on both sides of the car and a lighthouse at the end. One of Japan's designated top hundred scenic spots, and it earns it. Windy — take a jacket even here. 30 min from Hirara The other two

Kurima & Ikema bridges — 来間大橋 · 池間大橋 1,690 m and 1,425 m. Kurima gives the best single view of the full seven-kilometre sweep of Maehama from the hilltop viewpoint; Ikema opens up the wild northern tip, its wetland, and Nishihennazaki. Both under 20 min from town On the water

rows.text: Drive the three bridges anyway — heavy sky over that water is its own thing

Two compacts, not kei — トヨタレンタカー · C3クラス Booked with Toyota at the airport shop: two C3-class compacts , automatic, collected at 14:00 on the 21st. Two cars means the group splits without negotiating — divers one way, beach party the other — and unlike a kei they take six people and six suitcases in a single run on arrival day. 5 seats a car · a real boot · insurance already paid The great one

cards.text: Yoshino Kaigan — 吉野海岸 Fish swarm you the moment you're in, and a few metres further out the coral becomes a proper maze. The best reef you can reach straight off a beach anywhere on the island. Steep access path, reef shoes essential, and respect the current. East coast · pair with Aragusuku next door Tide-dependent

Toguchi-no-hama — 渡口の浜 A long, soft, curving stretch on Irabu that never seems to have anyone on it. No facilities to speak of, which is exactly why. Pair it with Makiyama Observatory and the drive back over the bridge. Irabu · combine with the bridge drive Closest to town

Clear SUP to the Pumpkin Rock — クリアSUP A transparent-hulled paddleboard over water this colour is faintly absurd, and the Pumpkin Rock — a limestone dome inside a sea cave, reachable only at the right tide — is the best two hours on the island that does not involve a tank. Around ¥7,000. Tide-dependent, so the operator picks the day, not you. Already pencilled for the 24th or 25th Free, and takes 20 minutes

cards.title: Sea turtle snorkelling
cards.text: Miyako’s green turtles sit in shallow, sheltered water and the operators here quote encounter rates at or near 100% — which, unusually for that kind of claim, is borne out by the reviews. No experience required, wetsuits provided, and most plans include hotel pickup and photos.
cards.book: Now that nobody is diving on the 24th, book this for all six as the morning of that day. Several operators bundle it with clear SUP for not much more, which would cover the whole day in one booking.
cards.when: Book a week or two out. Compare on the aggregator rather than going direct — the same boats are listed across all of them.
cards.meta: Length: half day · Cost: ≈ ¥6,000–8,000 · Suits: complete beginners · Pickup: usually included

cards.title: Pumpkin Rock kayak & SUP
cards.text: Paddle to a limestone sea cave holding a huge pumpkin-shaped formation. Usually bundled with reef snorkelling. The Shimajiri mangrove paddle is the calmer alternative.
cards.book: Ask your dive shop first — most Miyako operators run these or will point you at whoever does. Otherwise book through Activity Japan.
cards.when: Slot it on the 25th, your no-fly day.
cards.meta: Length: half day · Effort: low · Suits: everyone

cards.text: Toriike — 通り池 A national natural monument: two inland ponds connected to the open sea by a submerged tunnel, cave ceilings around 23 m and depths past 40 m. The hardest of the three, and it only goes on days when conditions and the whole team's skills line up. 40 m+ · a true cave · 50+ logged dives Your headline dive

Nakanoshima Channel — 中の島チャネル Shallow, bright and forgiving — a sand channel between reef walls with excellent light. Comfortably inside your 18 m limit, and the site to ask for by name on the 22nd. Good enough that shops run it for experienced divers too, which is the point. 5–18 m · inside your limit · also snorkellable Yes, on an OW card

Wonderful Cave & Mini Grotto — ワンダーホール周辺 The shallower end of the Shimoji cave menu — swim-throughs and grottoes with plenty of ambient light, giving the same cathedral feeling as the Big 3 without the depth or the commitment. ~15–20 m · light all the way, exit in sight Everyone

Yabiji reef — 八重干瀬 Japan's largest coral reef, a national natural monument, ~15 km north of Ikema. Trips run when the tides allow. The colour-and-fish day rather than the rock-formation day — good for divers and snorkellers on one boat. Tide-dependent · great for mixed groups Three Hirara names, four dinners Every dinner on the island is a short walk in Hirara, and the good rooms book out. Akagara (あかがーら) — Miy

Yonaha Maehama — 与那覇前浜 Seven kilometres of powder-fine white sand on the south-west coast, routinely ranked the best sand beach in Japan. Shallow, calm, and facing exactly the right way for sunset. This is your default evening. Sunset ~18:05 · watersports base Most photographed

Sunayama Beach — 砂山ビーチ Reached by climbing over a pine-topped sand dune, which is half the fun — then a small cove with a natural rock arch framing the sea. Compact and gets busy, so go early or at golden hour. 10 min from Hirara · short dune climb Best snorkelling

Painagama — パイナガマビーチ Walking distance from Hirara, so it's the locals' beach — showers, shade, a shop, and the place to take a beer at the end of a driving day without committing to a drive. In Hirara · easy sunset

rows.text: Guide-Ya-San — ガイド屋さん Built for exactly where you now are. Caps at four guests per guide , so six of you means two guides, and runs a named “Dive Together Tour for Certified Divers and Beginners” . Eighteen years accident-free. With the course off the table this is the better room — it is designed around diving Open Water divers well rather than around upgrading them. Ratio 4 guests per guide Mixed levels explic
Move dive days. Tell the shop early. You can slide a lost day onto the 24th and still be well clear of the flight — swap the turtles to the 25th if you do

Devil's Palace — 魔王の宮殿 Three chambers including the "altar" and the "bedroom", entered through a hole that admits one diver at a time, then a pitch-black passage that opens into shafts of blue light. The signature Miyako dive, ~30 min by boat beside Shimoji airport — and the reason people come back with an Advanced card. ~25 m · below your 18 m limit Out of reach this trip

Antonio Gaudí — アントニオガウディ West side of Shimoji. A collapsed reef structure of intricate arches and towers that genuinely looks architected — hence the name. Deeper and more exposed than Devil's Palace, and the most condition-dependent of the three. 30 m+ · well below your limit Out of reach this trip

Aquatic Adventure — 宮古島ダイビング アクアティックアドベンチャー Takes Open Water divers happily and runs a good modern boat. It also teaches the Advanced course — which you have decided against , so that advantage no longer applies and this drops behind Guide-Ya-San. Still a perfectly good booking for two shallow days if the other is full. Takes intro → advanced Boat Estrella de Agua, 2023 Your plan 2 days, no course Watch: Reviews call

BIGHOLIDAY — 宮古島ファンダイビング専門店 A superb fun-diving-only specialist, and the source of the difficulty tiering used on this page — but not available to you . Kept here so you know it was considered and why it was dropped, rather than wondering later. Minimum 30 logged dives Your group Open Water Verdict not this trip Why it is out: their words — “Participants must have 30 or more dives under their belt and be able

Penguin Divers — ペンギンダイバーズ Owner Yumiko runs it with her husband Joe, who is Fijian and a native English speaker — the only shop of the four where English is a first language rather than a service. Small-group and personal, and the one to pick if any of the six wants a briefing with no ambiguity in it. English native speaker Size small groups Style personal, guided Base Shimozato, Hirara Watch: The smallest operat

cards.text: Kiritanpo nabe — きりたんぽ鍋 Freshly cooked rice pounded smooth, moulded around cedar skewers, grilled over coals, then cut into a hot pot of Hinai-jidori chicken broth with burdock, maitake and seri — the whole plant, roots included, which is the local signature. Autumn and winter only. 27 or 28 Oct · ask the inn ahead Lunch

Inaniwa udon — 稲庭うどん One of Japan's three great udon and nothing like thick Sanuki: hand-stretched, flattened and air-dried into a pale, unusually silky noodle. Served cold with a dipping sauce even in autumn — have it that way first, because the texture is the entire point. 27 Oct · Kakunodate In town

Sake at the source — 日本酒 Akita's cold winters and soft water make it one of the top brewing prefectures. Suzuki Shuzo has made Hideyoshi in Kakunodate since 1689 and sits right on the samurai walk; Ando Jozo 's miso and soy warehouse is a few doors along, its brick storehouse worth entering on its own. 27 Oct afternoon · both walkable The local bird

Hinai-jidori — 比内地鶏 One of Japan's three great heritage chickens, raised only in northern Akita and far denser and more flavoured than ordinary bird. It's what makes kiritanpo broth taste like anything — but also worth eating on its own as oyakodon or grilled. Any meal here Winter preserve

Yamai ryori — The Nyuto inns serve mountain food that matches the bath: river fish grilled whole on skewers around a hearth, wild mountain vegetables, mushrooms, and miso hotpots. If you're doing day-use bathing, several will also serve lunch — worth asking when you phone about the bath. 28 Oct · book with the bath See every dish across the trip → ← Miyakojima Next · Aomori →

rows.title: Ando Jozo · miso & soy brewery
rows.text: A working miso and soy-sauce brewery in a Meiji-era brick storehouse on the main street. You can walk into the warehouse itself, which is the point.
rows.book: Free entry to the shop and warehouse. Buy the miso — it travels.
rows.when: Nothing to reserve. Open through the afternoon.
rows.meta: Founded: 19th century · Free: to walk in

rows.title: Suzuki Shuzo · Hideyoshi sake
rows.text: One of Akita’s long-standing breweries, making Hideyoshi in Kakunodate itself, a few doors from Ando Jozo. Akita’s cold winters and soft water are why this prefecture brews as well as it does.
rows.book: Shop is walk-in for tasting and buying. Brewery tours, if running, need arranging ahead — ask the tourist office by the station.
rows.when: Ask about tours a few days out if anyone wants one.

rows.text: Iburigakko — いぶりがっこ Daikon hung in the rafters over a smouldering fire, smoked for days, then pickled in rice bran — a solution to Akita winters too cold and dark to sun-dry anything. Smoky, sweet, crunchy. Best served with cream cheese and sake, which sounds wrong and isn't. Order alongside everything At the onsen

cards.title: Lake Tazawa cruise
cards.sub: and your inn is on the shore
cards.text: Japan’s deepest lake at 423 m — which is why it never freezes and why the blue is that improbable. Your dates catch the very end of the season, so this is a now-or-not-this-trip item. Katakurinohana sits on the lake, so it is a short drive rather than an outing.
cards.book: Confirm it is still sailing when you ring the inn about the late check-in — the closing date moves with the weather each year, and 2026 timings are published as a PDF.
cards.when: Best slotted into the 28th after Nyuto, or the morning of the 29th before you drive north.
cards.meta: Season: late Apr – early Nov · Length: ~40 min · Cost: ≈ ¥1,200 · From: Shirahama pier

cards.title: Tsurunoyu Onsen · day bathing
cards.text: Thatched buildings, milky-white sulphur water, and a large mixed open-air bath. The most famous bath in Tohoku.
cards.book: Phone reservation advised — day-use capacity is limited and it is taken by phone, in Japanese. Closed Monday mornings for cleaning; your Wednesday is fine. If full, Taenoyu faces a waterfall and Kuroyu and Ganiba are both excellent.
cards.when: Ring a few weeks out. Ask the inn at Katakurinohana to call for you if the language is a barrier.

cards.title: Aoyagi-ke samurai house
cards.text: The grandest of the Kakunodate samurai residences — a compound of several small museums, an armoury and gardens behind a black wooden gate.
cards.book: Walk-in, pay at the gate. Allow an hour; it is bigger inside than it looks from the street.
cards.when: Nothing to reserve.
cards.meta: Entry: ¥500 · Contains: armour, museums, gardens

cards.title: Taenoyu
cards.text: Arguably the more beautiful bath of the two — an open-air pool looking straight at a waterfall, with two different spring sources. The one to take if Tsurunoyu is full.
cards.book: Day bathing in a narrow window, 10:30–14:00. Ring ahead; capacity is small.
cards.when: Have this number with you on the 28th as the live fallback.
cards.meta: Day use: 10:30–14:00 · Price: ¥800 · Bath: faces a waterfall

cards.title: Kuroyu Onsen
cards.text: Thatched buildings and milky sulphur water, with the widest day-use window in the valley — the practical choice if you arrive later than planned.
cards.book: Day bathing 09:00–16:00, ¥600. No reservation needed for day use.
cards.when: No booking. The safety net if the morning overruns.
cards.meta: Day use: 09:00–16:00 · Price: ¥600 · Water: sulphurous, cloudy

cards.title: Ganiba Onsen
cards.text: The quietest of the group, with an open-air bath set among beech trees a short walk from the building. Least visited, and in late October that is the whole appeal.
cards.book: Day bathing 09:00–15:30, ¥600. Walk-in.
cards.when: No booking.
cards.meta: Day use: 09:00–15:30 · Price: ¥600 · Feature: beech-forest rotenburo

cards.text: Nyuto Onsen — rain makes an open-air bath better, not worse
Aoyagi-ke and Ishiguro-ke — the samurai houses are interiors

Nyuto Onsen — 乳頭温泉郷 Seven independent hot springs in mountain forest, each with different water. Tsurunoyu — thatched roofs, milky sulphur water, a big mixed open-air bath — is the famous one, day-use ~10:00–15:00 for ¥600–700, phone booking advised. Taenoyu faces a waterfall; Kuroyu and Ganiba are quieter and excellent. 28 Oct · arrive by 14:00 In town · 2 h

Bukeyashiki-dori — 武家屋敷通り An unusually intact samurai quarter: a broad street of black wooden walls and gates, with several houses open to walk through. Aoyagi-ke holds armour and a proper museum; Ishiguro-ke is the oldest and still lived in by the family. The weeping cherries that make it famous in spring turn gold in late October. 27 Oct afternoon · flat, easy Only here

rows.title: Ishiguro-ke samurai house
rows.sub: 27 Oct · the oldest, still lived in
rows.text: The oldest surviving samurai house in Kakunodate, and the only one where the family still lives upstairs. Smaller than Aoyagi-ke and considerably more atmospheric for it.
rows.book: Walk-in. Opening hours are shorter than Aoyagi-ke and can vary — check on the day.
rows.when: Nothing to reserve, but go before 16:00.
rows.meta: Entry: small charge · Age: oldest in the district · Note: family still resides

cards.title: Dakigaeri Gorge
cards.sub: 27 Oct · peak foliage on your dates
cards.text: Ten kilometres of gorge along a mineral blue-green river, maples right over the water, a red suspension bridge and the Kaiun-no-taki waterfall. The single best walk of the trip and it costs nothing.
cards.book: No entry fee and nothing to reserve. Parking fills with coach traffic from mid-morning — the only booking that matters is your own start time.
cards.when: Be there by 09:15. A Tuesday morning in season is as quiet as it gets.
cards.meta: Entry: free · Drive: 15 min from town · Walk: 1.5–4 h · Festival: runs in season

cards.text: Lake Tazawa shore — 田沢湖 Japan's deepest lake at 423 m, which is why it holds that cobalt colour year-round. Short level walks to the gilded Tatsuko statue standing in the shallows and the red Gozanoishi Shrine torii on the north shore. Drivable loop with pull-offs the whole way. 28 Oct · easy track Drive + 1–1.5 h walk

Oyasukyo Daifunto — 小安峡大噴湯 A short staircase into a narrow gorge where superheated steam and boiling water blast horizontally out of cracks in the rock face, right beside the path. Loud, hot and slightly alarming. Also at peak colour in late October. ~1.5 h south · optional detour Easy · birch forest

Nyuto Kogen trails — 乳頭高原 Gentle paths linking the seven hot springs through beech and birch, with no altitude risk and colour the whole way. The right choice if Komagatake is snowed off but the active four still want to walk before the bath. 28 Oct fallback · all abilities
Skip the summit. Komagatake in cloud is a car park with no view — swap it, do not push it
Lake Tazawa by car — the loop works from the car in any weather

Loop the lake, do not cut across — 田沢湖一周・県道38号 Your inn sits on the western shore and the road outside it goes all the way round — about 20 km, thirty to forty minutes without stopping . It passes the gilded Tatsuko statue on the west shore and Gozanoishi shrine on the north, where a torii stands in the water. Any trip from the inn can begin with a half or full circuit rather than joining Route 46 straight away. On a clear morning

Route 341, the mountain way north — 国道341号 The road that matters on the 29th. Rather than dropping onto the expressway, Route 341 runs north from Tazawako through the mountains to Kazuno — Japanese drivers describe it as a superb mountain route with very little traffic, which is precisely what an expressway is not. It threads two dam lakes: Akisen-ko , then Hosen-ko below the Tamagawa dam, whose water is an extraordinary lapis blue

Mt Akita-Komagatake — 秋田駒ヶ岳 · 1,637 m Drive up to the 8th Station at ~1,300 m — private cars are unrestricted after 20 October and the road stays open until 1 November — then walk the crater rim. Huge views over Tazawa and Hachimantai. Snow is the only variable; check on the morning. 28 Oct · moderate · road shuts 1 Nov Easy · flat

Hachimantai Aspite Line — 八幡平アスピーテライン Twenty-seven kilometres straight over the top of the Hachimantai massif, with an easy crater-lake and marsh boardwalk from the summit car park. Closes in early November , so late October is the last of it. Watch for night closures and early snow. 28 Oct alternative · check before driving Easy · steamy

cards.title: Kabazaiku Denshokan
cards.text: Wild cherry bark shaved, polished and laminated onto tea caddies and boxes until it glows reddish-brown. Invented here by low-ranking samurai as a side income. Craftsmen work on site.
cards.book: Walk-in. The shop sells the real thing — tea caddies are the buy, and they last decades.
cards.when: Nothing to reserve.
cards.meta: Craft: exists only here · Age: ~2 centuries · Watch: artisans at work

cards.text: Kabazaiku cherry-bark craft — 樺細工 Wild cherry bark, polished until it looks like lacquered stone, worked into tea caddies and boxes. It was the off-season handwork of Kakunodate’s samurai and it is still made nowhere else. The Denshokan on the samurai street has live demonstrations and short hands-on sessions, and the tea caddies are the one souvenir from this trip worth carrying home. Tax-free over ¥5,000 with your passport T

cards.title: Furukawa market · nokkedon
cards.text: Buy a bowl of rice and a book of tickets, then walk the stalls trading tickets for scallop, uni, tuna and roe. You build the bowl yourself.
cards.book: No booking. Just turn up early with cash.
cards.when: Check the weekly closing day before you plan the 1st around it.
cards.meta: Walk: 5 min from hotel · Mornings: only

cards.text: Hotate & kaiyaki-miso — 帆立・貝焼き味噌 Aomori grows more scallops than anywhere in Japan and the season starts now. Best as kaiyaki-miso — scallop and egg cooked with miso in a big shell used as the pan, a Tsugaru fishermen's dish. Sweet, rich, and served everywhere from markets to izakayas. 1 Nov · last dinner Local rarity

Apples, in every form — りんご Aomori grows over half of Japan's apples, centred on Hirosaki, and late October is harvest. The tourist office maps around fifty distinct local apple pies . Then there's the hard cider poured at A-Factory on the Aomori waterfront, with a tasting flight of four. 31 Oct Hirosaki · A-Factory any evening Hachinohe

Senbei-jiru — せんべい汁 Wheat crackers made specifically to be boiled, broken into a chicken or pork broth with vegetables where they go chewy rather than soggy. A frugal Nambu dish turned regional icon, and exactly what you want after a cold day at Hakkoda. Cold days · widely available If you go to Shimokita

Ōma tuna — 大間まぐろ The most famous bluefin in Japan, line-caught one fish at a time off the northern tip of the Shimokita peninsula — the ones that break auction records at Toyosu. Eating it at the port where it lands is a genuinely different proposition from eating it in Tokyo. 31 Oct · only on the Osorezan track See every dish across the trip → ← Kakunodate Pre-departure plan →

rows.text: Ichigo-ni — いちご煮 Sea urchin and abalone in a clear dashi, named because the urchin suspended in the cloudy broth looks like wild strawberries. A Hachinohe festival dish and one of the more expensive things you'll eat — worth ordering once, properly, on the last night. 1 Nov · order it once Everywhere

cards.title: Apple picking · Hirosaki Apple Park
cards.sub: and you are here at peak Fuji
cards.text: Aomori grows more than half of Japan’s apples, and picking runs to mid-November — which puts you squarely in Fuji season, the best of them and the last to ripen. Around eighty varieties in the park.
cards.book: No booking needed. Slots straight into the 31st alongside Hirosaki Castle and the cider, which is the strongest version of that day.
cards.when: Confirm the picking is still running that week — it depends on the harvest, not the calendar.
cards.meta: Season: 1 Aug – mid-Nov · Cost: a few hundred yen · Varieties: ~80 · Where: Hirosaki, ~1 hr

cards.title: Tsugaru-jamisen, live
cards.sub: Hirosaki · the best evening on this leg
cards.text: Forget the polite image of shamisen — Tsugaru style is percussive, furiously fast, and played a metre from your table while you eat Tsugaru food. Most visitors never think to do this, and it is the thing people remember about Aomori years later.
cards.book: Three venues in Hirosaki do it properly: Anzu, Aiya and Adohadari. Rooms are small — book a table for six rather than turning up.
cards.when: Pairs with the 31st if you take the Hirosaki option, since you are already there.
cards.meta: Where: Anzu, Aiya, Adohadari · Cost: dinner + cover · Sets: through the evening · Book: yes, small rooms

cards.title: A-Factory cidre works
cards.text: A glass-walled cider works in the harbour building — you watch it being made, then drink it. Kimori and the house flight run dry through to sweet, all from Aomori apples. Also the best place in the city to buy apple everything.
cards.book: No booking. The obvious use of a spare hour before dinner on any of the four Aomori evenings.
cards.when: Walkable from Art Hotel Aomori, so it survives bad weather and tired legs.
cards.meta: Cost: tasting flight · Length: ~1 hr · Where: harbour, by the station · Open: late

cards.title: Tsugaru-han Neputa Village
cards.text: Neputa floats, live shamisen through the day, craft demonstrations, and goldfish-neputa painting you can take home. Not high art, but a genuinely good two hours if the 31st turns wet and the mountain roads shut.
cards.book: Walk in. Worth holding in reserve rather than planning — it is the fallback that makes a bad-weather 31st fine instead of wasted.
cards.when: Next to the castle park, so it combines with the apples and the cider.
cards.meta: Length: ~2 hrs · Where: beside Hirosaki Castle · Indoors: entirely

cards.title: Sukayu Onsen · thousand-person bath
cards.text: A vast all-hinoki mixed bathing hall of roughly 260 m². Acidic, milky, and the classic Hakkoda soak — fifteen minutes from the ropeway.
cards.book: Day bathing is walk-in, no reservation needed. Ring only if you want lunch or a room. Note the women-only hour if that matters to anyone.
cards.when: No booking. Just turn up between the ropeway and the drive home.
cards.meta: Hiba Sennin-buro: 07:00–18:00 · Women only: 08:00–09:00 · Tama-no-yu: 09:00–17:00

cards.title: Aoni Onsen · the lamp inn
cards.text: No electricity by design — lit entirely by oil lamps. Four baths, including a riverside open-air reached across a suspension bridge. Genuinely unlike anywhere else you will go.
cards.book: Day bathing is available in the daytime, but the road in is narrow and remote — phone ahead to confirm they are open to day visitors that day. Staying the night is also possible and is the fuller experience.
cards.when: Ring a week out. Pairs with the Hirosaki day.
cards.meta: Light: oil lamps only · Baths: 4, free-flowing · Access: narrow mountain road

cards.title: Nebuta Warasse
cards.text: Five of the previous year’s prize-winning Nebuta floats, lit and at close range — twenty-odd feet of painted washi warriors on wire frames.
cards.book: Walk-in, tickets at the door. No reservation.
cards.when: Any evening. Best paired with A-Factory next door for Aomori cider.
cards.meta: Walk: 5 min from hotel · Indoors: year-round

cards.title: Sannai-Maruyama
cards.text: A Jomon settlement occupied for more than a thousand years, with reconstructed pit dwellings and the great six-pillar timber tower. The best bad-weather day in the prefecture.
cards.book: Walk-in. Free guided tours run through the day — ask at the desk when you arrive, they are worth catching.
cards.when: No booking. Combine with the art museum next door.
cards.meta: Drive: 20 min · Mostly: under cover · Next to: the art museum

cards.title: Osorezan Bodaiji
cards.sub: 31 Oct · last day of the season
cards.text: One of the three holiest sites in Japan — a sulphur-blasted crater of grey ash and steaming vents beside a startlingly blue caldera lake, understood as the entrance to the underworld.
cards.book: Walk-in entry. It shuts on 31 October until May, so ring first to confirm the final day’s hours before committing five hours of driving.
cards.when: Decide by the 30th. There is no second chance on this trip.
cards.meta: Season: 1 May – 31 Oct · Drive: 2 h 30 each way · On site: free onsen huts

cards.title: Lake Towada cruise
cards.text: A boat across the caldera lake. Its real use is logistical: sail one way and walk Oirase the other, so nobody backtracks.
cards.book: Tickets at the pier. Check the 2026 timetable before you plan the day around it — season dates and the last sailing move each year.
cards.when: Confirm the timetable the week before.
cards.meta: Route: Yasumiya ↔ Nenokuchi · Pairs with: walking Oirase one way

cards.title: Hirosaki Park · autumn festival
cards.text: The Chrysanthemum and Autumn Foliage Festival runs across your dates, with the maples lit after dark. Check whether the castle keep is back on its stone base after the wall repairs before you build the day around it.
cards.book: Park entry is walk-in; the festival area has a small charge. The tourist association publishes the apple-pie map — pick it up at the station or download it.
cards.when: Nothing to reserve, but confirm the festival dates and the keep’s status the week before.
cards.meta: Festival: mid-Oct → early Nov · Drive: 45 min · Also: ~50 mapped apple pies

cards.text: Hirosaki — castle park, Western architecture and fifty apple pies

rows.title: Aomori Museum of Art
rows.sub: 1 Nov · next to the Jomon site
rows.text: Yoshitomo Nara’s four-storey Aomori-ken dog, Shiko Munakata’s woodblocks, and Chagall’s vast painted backdrops for Aleko. One of the best regional museums in Japan.
rows.book: Walk-in. Check the weekly closing day and whether an exhibition changeover is on before you drive out.
rows.when: No booking, but confirm opening on the day.
rows.meta: Drive: 20 min · Holds: Nara, Munakata, Chagall

rows.text: Asamushi aquarium — twenty minutes east, fine in a downpour

cards.title: Hakkoda Ropeway
cards.text: A 100-person cabin to Tamoyachi-dake. By 30 Oct the summit itself will likely be bare or frosted — the range views and the road up are the real payoff.
cards.book: No advance booking — buy at the station. But it stops for high wind as often as for snow, so ring on the morning before you commit to the hour’s drive.
cards.when: Call the morning of, from the hotel.
cards.meta: First car: 09:00 · Every: 15–20 min · Last down: 16:40 · Top: 1,324 m

cards.text: Oirase Gorge — 奥入瀬渓流 Fourteen kilometres of stream running out of Lake Towada past moss, rapids and a dozen named waterfalls, on a level path the whole way. Walk any length you like. With two cars, drop one carload at Nenokuchi and collect them at Ishigedo — the classic middle section, and the best use of having a driver. 29 Oct · peak foliage mid-Oct to early Nov Easy · ~1 h

Hakkoda summit boardwalk — 八甲田 Straight off the ropeway at 1,324 m: a marked, level boardwalk loop across the alpine plateau with views over the whole range. No navigation, no scrambling — but exposed and genuinely cold by late October, so proper layers. 30 Oct · all abilities Easy · ~40 min

Juniko & Aoike — 十二湖・青池 Thirty-three lakes (despite the name) scattered through UNESCO beech forest. Aoike is the reason to come — a small pond of impossible glowing cobalt whose colour still isn't fully explained. Level paths link the main lakes. 31 Oct · 2h drive each way Moderate · ~3 h

Anmon Falls — 暗門の滝 The real Shirakami walk: a river-gorge trail with boardwalks and crossings leading to three stacked waterfalls, through the largest virgin beech forest in East Asia. Wet underfoot and gear is sometimes required — confirm the trail's open this late. 31 Oct · for the active four Hard · 4–5 h

Mt Odake — 大岳 · 1,585 m The proper Hakkoda traverse, from the ropeway over the high ground and down past the sulphur vents at Jigoku-numa to Sukayu Onsen. Superb, but snow is likely by 30 October and it turns into a winter mountain fast — check conditions and be willing to turn back. 30 Oct · conditions-dependent

Tsuta-numa pond loop — 蔦沼 Six ponds linked by a level path through old beech forest. Tsuta-numa itself produces the mirror reflection that is one of the most photographed autumn scenes in Japan — and it's only glass early, before the wind gets up. Worth an early start. 30 Oct · easy · go at dawn Easy · 60–90 min

cards.title: Tsugaru Iwaki Skyline
cards.text: A toll road up the flank of Mt Iwaki to the 8th station, then a chairlift to just below the 1,625 m summit. The biggest view-to-effort ratio in the region.
cards.book: Toll paid at the gate, no advance booking. But it closes for the season in early November and shuts in bad weather — ring to confirm the road and the chairlift are both running.
cards.when: Ring the morning of, before driving to Hirosaki.
cards.meta: Bends: 69 numbered hairpins · Then: chairlift to near summit · Closes: early November

cards.text: Hakka Pass, 631 m — 発荷峠展望台 The southern gateway to Lake Towada on Route 103, and the point where the caldera opens up beneath you — the lake, the Ohanabe headland, and the Hakkoda range beyond. Car park, shop and toilets, so it is the natural break on the drive north. Fifteen minutes on foot is Shimeitei , counted among Japan’s eight great views, and the angle from which Towada reads as a heart. Crater-rim foliage pe

Jogakura Ohashi — 城ヶ倉大橋 Japan’s largest deck-type arch bridge — 360 m long, a 255 m span, 122 m of gorge underneath — on Route 394 just west of the Hakkoda road. From the deck you get a genuine 360°: the Hakkoda peaks, Aomori city below, and Mount Iwaki away west. Its foliage peaks mid to late October , which is your window exactly — beech, maple and Erman’s birch, and after rain the colour comes off the water far

Mt Iwaki via the Skyline — 岩木山 · 1,625 m Drive 69 numbered hairpins to the 8th station, take a chairlift to the 9th, then walk the last rocky stretch to the summit of the mountain that dominates every view in Tsugaru. The biggest payoff-to-effort ratio in the region. Road closes early November. 31 Oct · pairs with Hirosaki Easy · 1–2 h

Hakkoda–Towada Gold Line — 国道103号 Aomori city up over the Hakkoda range past Sukayu and Jigoku-numa, down through Tsuta and along Oirase to Lake Towada. One of the most celebrated autumn drives in Japan and the backbone of both your 29th and your 30th. ~2h without stops · you will stop Coastal

rows.text: Route 101, the Nihonkai coast — 日本海沿い Empty coastal highway along the Sea of Japan towards Shirakami, with the wave-cut rock shelf at Senjojiki and long unbroken views west. Best driven late, heading home with the sun going down over the water. 31 Oct · the approach to Juniko Indoor · 1 h

Kasamatsu Pass & Suiren-numa — 傘松峠・睡蓮沼 Route 103 tops out at 1,040 m at Kasamatsu Pass, and Suiren-numa sits right beside the road there. Five minutes along a boardwalk and the whole Hakkoda ridge stands reflected in the pond — the classic view of the range, for almost no walking. On the way to Sukayu — do not drive past it Flat · 1–5 h
